answer: The harbor multiplier is published, charged in tide, and pearl lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 2 for each member already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4602 identities would post 3436 proofs and burn roughly 31 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
